something up. as the unit 1 driver started to cross the cross walk the second female stood up and stepped off the curb. the driver said he wasn't going fast and he bumped into the female. the female fell to the ground. the driver got out of his truck and helped the female up and asked her if she was ok. the female didn't respond and walked away across the sidewalk east bound. the driver got back right ankle. lawson said her left shoulder hurt from where the grill of the truck hit her. there was a small red mark on her left shoulder. the female also mentioned that she was just in a bad wreck in nevada and she had a lawyer for that. per sgt. hall no citations were issued at this time.

records.deidentified_narrative: this is traffic fatality #32 for the city of dallas in 2017. see related [case id]. unit 2/pedestrian was walking w/b across [roadway], from the east sidewalk. unit 1 was traveling s/b [roadway] and collided front concentrated (front right) to unit 2/pedestrian right side of body. unit 2/pedestrian was thrown southbound for approximately 58 feet, then she slid for approximately another 89 [roadway] of s/b [roadway], before coming to rest. unit 1 left the location without stopping to render aid to unit 2/pedestrian. witness 1 joseph ctvrtlik was walking w/b across [roadway] with unit 2/pedestrian, but he stopped, before entering the s/b lanes of traffic and was not struck. witness 1 was interviewed by vcu det. 5786 and vcu det. 5529. unit 1 and unit 1 driver were located at a later time by vcu detectives and the information obtained was provided to i/o to include in this report. i/o was able to view surveillance video footage of the moments before the crash, as unit 2/pedestrian and [roadway]. i/o also viewed two videos from after the crash, one which showed unit 2/pedestrian body coming to rest, as unit 1 fled the scene and a second video which showed unit 1 leaving the scene of the crash. while watching the videos containing unit 1, i/o made the visual observation that unit 1 appeared to be traveling at a speed higher than the posted speed limit of 30 mph. i/o interviewed witness 2 (andre sevigny) at the scene and he said that he observed the crash. he said that prior to the crash he had heard tires squealing, then he heard a car accelerate. he said that unit 1 was going fast. i/o used the distance of unit 2/pedestrian travel from the aoi to rest, which was approximately 147 feet and placed the approximate distance into the searle pedestrian equation to determine a minimum speed for unit 1. the formula showed that unit 1 was traveling at a minimum speed of 53 mph in a 30 mph zone at the time of impact. this report is incomplete pending toxicology results for unit 2/pedestrian. [roadway] and 500 [roadway] both show to be streets on google maps, but they are both private drives and not official city streets, so i/o used [roadway] to the scene of the crash. ****** this report was supplemented on [date] by i/o #8502 to correct the initial impact from unit 1 to unit 2/pedestrian. the report showed that she was struck on the left side of her body, but she was actually struck on the right side of her body, [roadway] from east to west and unit 1 was traveling s/b. ****** ***** on [date], i/o #8502 supplemented this report to include the toxicology results for unit 2 pedestrian. the blood results showed that unit 2 pedestrian was positive for alcohol and a drug was detected. ethanol: 0. 245 +/- 0. 014 g/100ml and amphetamine was detected. the contributing factor of under the influence of alcohol was added to unit 2 pedestrian. this report is now complete. *****

approximately another 89 [roadway] of s/b [roadway], before coming to rest. unit 1 left the location without stopping to render aid to unit 2/pedestrian. witness 1 joseph ctvrtlik was walking w/b across [roadway] with unit 2/pedestrian, but he stopped, before entering the s/b lanes of traffic and was not struck. witness 1 was interviewed by vcu det. 5786 and vcu det. 5529. unit 1 and unit 1 driver were located at a later time by vcu detectives and the information obtained was provided to i/o to include in this report. i/o was able to view surveillance video footage of the moments before the crash, as unit 2/pedestrian and [roadway]. i/o also viewed two videos from after the crash, one which showed unit 2/pedestrian body coming to rest, as unit 1 fled the scene and a second video which showed unit 1 leaving the scene of the crash. while watching the videos containing unit 1, i/o made the visual observation that unit 1 appeared to be traveling at a speed higher than the posted speed limit of 30 mph. i/o interviewed witness 2 (andre sevigny) at the scene and he said that he observed the crash. he said that prior to the crash he had heard tires squealing, then he heard a car accelerate. he said that unit 1 was going fast. i/o used the distance of unit 2/pedestrian travel from the aoi to rest, which was approximately 147 feet and placed the approximate distance into the searle pedestrian equation to determine a minimum speed for unit 1. the formula showed that unit 1 was traveling at a minimum speed of 53 mph in a 30 mph zone at the time of impact. this report is incomplete pending toxicology results for unit 2/pedestrian. [roadway] and 500 [roadway] both show to be streets on google maps, but they are both private drives and not official city streets, so i/o used [roadway] to the scene of the crash. ****** this report was supplemented on [date] by i/o #8502 to correct the initial impact from unit 1 to unit 2/pedestrian. the report showed that she was struck on the left side of her body, but she was actually struck on the right side of her body, [roadway] from east to west and unit 1 was traveling s/b. ****** ***** on [date], i/o #8502 supplemented this report to include the toxicology results for unit 2 pedestrian. the blood results showed that unit 2 pedestrian was positive for alcohol and a drug was detected. ethanol: 0. 245 +/- 0. 014 g/100ml and amphetamine was detected. the contributing factor of under the influence of alcohol was added to unit 2 pedestrian. this report is now complete. *****
